analyst: Manual analysis using Claude Opus 5.5 for verification and code analysis

servers.code_repo: Cloud server closed; local server for EU/Federal (different, generated): https://github.com/launchdarkly/mcp-server
servers.mcp_version: Cloud: not published. Local: TypeScript SDK 1.27.1
servers.commit_hash: e4a35c6f6ec2ec16bfa84cf8e6ea838249c239d5 (local server v0.7.1; cloud not applicable)
servers.linked_cost: Developer $0 (unlimited seats, 1K client-side MAU, 5 service connections, 5K AI runs); Foundation $10 per service connection/month, $8.33 per 1K MAU (also $10 on the page), $5 per extra 1K AI runs; Enterprise on request
servers.restrictions: Rights = the rights of the member who authorized the connection (role changes immediate; removed members lose access); Writer/Developer for writing, Reader for reading; environment approval processes apply to MCP; cloud server not available for federal environments and the EU instance; toolsets/writes URL parameters narrow the visible tools.
servers.restricted_by: LaunchDarkly administrator (roles, approval processes), user (toolsets/writes in the URL)
servers.governance_logic: 1) confirm=true required for irreversible deletions (delete-flag, delete-ai-config, delete-ai-config-variation, delete-dataset, delete-prompt-snippet, delete-agent-graph, delete-agent-skill, delete-alert, delete-dashboard). 2) delete-flag requires verdict safe from check-removal-readiness. 3) delete-agent-skill blocked while attached to a variation. 4) Built-in approval processes; apply-approval-request applies only human-approved changes. 5) Archive as a soft alternative. 6) Query limits (query-traces <= 24 h; get-doc <= 75 KB, only launchdarkly.com/docs/). 7) update-release-autopilot-settings sends only changed fields, autoCleanup forbidden. 8) New flags start OFF in all environments. 9) destructive/read-only annotations. 10) toolsets/writes filtering (does not change rights). 11) vent tool and server instructions promoting LaunchDarkly skills. 12) Deprecated factory-* duplicates left in the list.
servers.structure_note: Several endpoints on one host: /mcp/v1 (CSV, 18 tools), /mcp/launchdarkly (documented, 170 tools), /mcp/fm (111 tools); flat lists with toolset filtering; agent skills distributed separately and also managed as product objects
servers.actions_comment: CSV endpoint /mcp/v1: 18 (listed on the Actions sheet). Documented server /mcp/launchdarkly: 170 (166 names established, see 18_launchdarkly.md); /mcp/fm: 111.
servers.token_method: Full tools/list not available; with 170 tools the context is very large (hence toolsets)
servers.agent_cannot: Manage roles and teams (only invitations), integrations, billing; work in EU/Federal via the cloud server. On /mcp/v1 additionally: no flag deletion/archiving, no AI Configs, observability, segments, vent.
servers.docs_recs: "Review tool calls before your AI client runs them, especially calls that change or delete data"; "Don't set your AI client to approve these calls automatically"; disconnect the server after work and revoke access.
servers.gov_promises: Results go to the AI provider; LaunchDarkly "doesn't control your AI client or your model provider". Explicit list of what may be sent: flags, segments, AI Configs, change history, approval request descriptions, contexts and attributes (may contain end-user personal data), observability data incl. sessions, member names and e-mails, server-side SDK keys. Prompt injection warning: "anyone who can write data that MCP tools return can try to give instructions to the model".
servers.user_promises: Hosted server is "more feature complete" than the local one
servers.promises_vs_logic: Some risks covered by the server (confirm=true, readiness check, skill deletion blocking, approvals); others left to the user (review calls, no auto-approval). New session-recording and context tools increase personal data going to the AI provider; no masking declared.
servers.notes: Analysis 16.10.2026, re-analysed 21.10.2026 after a new commit in the repository; the description reflects the state as of 21.10.2026. The CSV endpoint /mcp/v1 is a separate small server (18 tools, own OAuth metadata, scopes reader/writer); the documentation describes /mcp/launchdarkly. The Actions sheet lists the 18 tools of the CSV endpoint; the 166 established names of /mcp/launchdarkly are in 18_launchdarkly.md. Server pages hosted via Speakeasy.

Tools.desc: /mcp/v1 (CSV): 18 tools (feature flags and approvals). /mcp/launchdarkly: 170 tools. Annotations Read-only / Idempotent / Destructive for most.
Tools.pre: Short descriptions and annotations on the install pages; full tools/list not published
Tools.post: Not documented as a whole. check-removal-readiness returns safe/caution/blocked; segments return requiresApproval: true; get-session-event-chunk-url returns a signed link valid ~15 minutes

Authorization.desc: OAuth only (no API keys); access token 2 h with refresh; re-authorization every 90 days. /mcp/v1 metadata: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/v1; authorization server app.launchdarkly.com/trust/oauth (authorize, token, revoke); DCR (/trust/oauth/register/dcr); grants authorization_code, refresh_token, client_credentials; PKCE S256; scopes reader, writer
Authorization.src: mcp-hosted docs; OAuth metadata (retrieved by a script)

Configuration.desc: toolsets and writes URL parameters filter the visible tools ("These parameters don't limit what the connection can do in your account")

Other.desc: Server instructions: "IMPORTANT: Before using tools, check if the environment has LaunchDarkly related agent skills or SKILL.md installed"; then the agent is asked to ask the user whether to install skills from launchdarkly/ai-tooling

actions.desc: Get the health of a flag
Get a flag's status across environments
Check whether a flag can be removed (verdict safe / caution / blocked)
Create a feature flag (starts OFF in all environments)
Toggle a flag on/off (may require approval; marked Destructive on /mcp/v1)
Copy a flag configuration between environments (Destructive)
Create an approval request for a change
Apply a change that has been approved by a human (Destructive)

observations.text: The most honest documentation about risks in the sample: lists which data goes to the AI provider and explains prompt injection through data.
Multi-level protection of deletion: confirm=true + verdict safe + blocking when there are dependencies + preference for archiving - closest to server-side "refusal conditions" from the task.
Integration with the product's human approval processes: the agent can only request approval and apply the change after a human approved it.
Vendor interests: vent (agent as a source of product feedback, like tavily_feedback) and server instructions suggesting LaunchDarkly skills.
Skills in three roles: distributed outside the server (repository), recommended through server instructions and managed by the agent as product objects.
Deprecated duplicate tools (Factory <-> Release Autopilot) are left in the list - extra context and risk of confusion.
Toolsets via the URL control the context size and the set of actions.
Secrets (SDK keys) handed out to the agent via get-project / get-environment.
The CSV endpoint /mcp/v1 is a separate small server (18 tools) while the documentation describes /mcp/launchdarkly (170): several official servers on one host.
